questions.question: Q: What is the difference between binary and ternary form?
questions.correctAnswer: Binary form has two sections (A B), while ternary form has three (A B A) where the opening section returns after the contrast.

questions.question: Q: Describe the structure of a rondo and give its pattern.
questions.correctAnswer: A rondo has a main theme that keeps returning, alternating with different contrasting episodes, following the pattern ABACADA.

questions.question: Q: How does an abstract structure differ from a narrative structure?
questions.correctAnswer: A narrative structure tells a story with characters and events in order; an abstract structure is organised around movement ideas and qualities without a storyline.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Dance Structure & Form

questions.question: Q: Why might a choreographer choose ternary form for their dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Ternary form gives a sense of balance and resolution because the opening section returns, providing familiarity. The middle section offers contrast before the return creates a satisfying conclusion.

questions.question: Q: Explain what a thematic structure is and how it works.
questions.correctAnswer: A thematic structure is built around one or more movement themes that are developed and varied throughout the piece. The themes reappear in different forms, creating unity while maintaining interest.
